Houses are cleaned, painted footprints lead the goddess in from the door, and rows of lamps and candles are lit on sills, roofs and steps so that she will enter. Girls go from house to house singing bhailo.

KAKABALI.about: Kakabali, the offering to the crow, is a name for Kag Tihar, the first day of Tihar, on the thirteenth tithi of the dark half before Kartik's new moon. Crows, seen as messengers of Yama, god of death, are honoured with the first portion of the day's food, set out on leaf plates on roofs and in courtyards so that no sad news comes to the house.

DASHAIN_TIKA.about: Dashain Tika falls on Vijaya Dashami, the tenth tithi of the bright half of Ashwin, which recalls Durga's victory over the demon Mahishasura. At the auspicious hour elders give red tika of rice, curd and vermilion and the jamara grown since Ghatasthapana to younger relatives with blessings, and families visit their elders to receive tika for several days after.

PITRI_VISARJAN.about: Pitri Visarjan, the farewell to the ancestors, is the new-moon day that closes the sixteen days of Sorah Shraddha before Dashain. The ancestors, held to have come to their descendants during the fortnight, are offered a last shraddha of pinda and water, especially for those whose death date is unknown, and are bid farewell. Ghatasthapana follows the next day.

SANDHYA_ARGHYA.about: Sandhya Arghya, the evening offering, falls on the sixth tithi of the bright half of Kartik, the main day of Chhath. After a fast without water, those keeping the vow stand in a river or pond at dusk and offer arghya to the setting Sun and to Chhathi Maiya, with bamboo baskets of thekua, fruit and sugarcane carried to the bank by their families.

DALA_PUJA.about: Dala Puja, the worship of the baskets, is a name for the evening of the sixth tithi of Kartik's bright half during Chhath. Bamboo baskets, the dala and sup, are filled with thekua, fruits, sugarcane and lamps, worshipped at home and carried to the riverbank, where they are held up to the setting Sun as the arghya is given, while women sing Chhath songs.

USHA_ARGHYA.about: Usha Arghya, the dawn offering, falls on the seventh tithi of the bright half of Kartik, the last day of Chhath. Before sunrise those keeping the vow return to the river or pond and stand in the water to offer arghya to the rising Sun. They then break the fast of some thirty-six hours, and the prasad from the baskets is shared.

CHHATH_SAMAPAN.about: Chhath Samapan, the close of Chhath, is the morning of the seventh tithi of Kartik's bright half. When arghya has been given to the rising Sun at the riverbank, the four-day festival ends: those keeping the vow break their fast with prasad, and thekua and fruit from the baskets are shared among family and neighbours.

DARSHA_SHRADDHA.about: Darsha Shraddha is the shraddha of every new moon, the darsha, offered to the ancestors in the afternoon, the time the texts set for it. Householders who keep it offer water with sesame and pinda to three generations of forebears on each new moon of the year, and in Nepal several new moons, such as Kushe Aunsi and Gaya Aunsi, draw crowds to the tirthas.

SHUKLA_ASHTAMI_VRATA.about: The Shukla Ashtami Vrata is the fast of the eighth day of every bright half, kept above all for the goddess Durga. Those who keep it fast and worship the goddess, often at her temples; for a vow the texts take the later of two days when the eighth spans them. The eighths of Chaitra and Ashwin are the great Ashtamis of the two Navaratris.

KRISHNA_ASHTAMI_VRATA.about: The Krishna Ashtami Vrata is the fast of the eighth day of every dark half, which some keep for Kalabhairava, the fierce form of Shiva who guards Kashi. Those who keep it fast through the day and worship Bhairava in the evening, at the pradosha, the hour the texts set for this vow, often at his temples.

TULASI_ROPANA.about: Tulasi Ropana, the planting of tulasi, is kept on Harishayani Ekadashi in Ashadh's bright half, when Vishnu is held to lie down for his four months' sleep. Households plant a sapling of tulasi, the holy basil dear to Vishnu, in the courtyard's tulasi mound and worship it daily through the Chaturmas, until its marriage on Haribodhini Ekadashi in Kartik.

VYASA_JAYANTI.about: Vyasa Jayanti, the full moon of Ashadh, is kept as the birthday of Veda Vyasa, the sage held to have arranged the Vedas and composed the Mahabharata and the Puranas, and so is also Guru Purnima. Students and disciples worship Vyasa and honour their own teachers and gurus with gifts and their respect, and schools and monasteries mark the day.

SHUKLA_GORAKHKALI_PUJA.about: Gorakhkali Puja on the eighth day of the bright half is the worship of Gorakhkali, the goddess whose seat at the old palace of Gorkha is held as the lineage goddess of the Shah kings. The national panchanga marks it on the bright eighths, the day of the monthly Ashtami vow, when the goddess is worshipped at Gorkha and by those devoted to her.

KRISHNA_GORAKHKALI_PUJA.about: Gorakhkali Puja on the eighth day of the dark half is the worship of Gorakhkali, the lineage goddess of the Shah kings, whose seat is at the old palace of Gorkha. The national panchanga marks it on the dark eighths, the days of Bhairava's monthly vow, and her worship on Paush's dark eighth and on an eighth falling on Tuesday is held especially fitting.

WORLD_DAY_FOR_SAFETY_AND_HEALTH_AT_WORK.about: The World Day for Safety and Health at Work, on 28 April, has been kept by the International Labour Organization since 2003, on the same date as trade unions' day of remembrance for workers killed and injured at work. It promotes the prevention of accidents and diseases at work. In Nepal trade unions and employers mark it with programmes on workplace safety.

INTERNATIONAL_DAY_OF_INNOCENT_CHILDREN_V.about: The International Day of Innocent Children Victims of Aggression falls on 4 June. The UN General Assembly set it in August 1982, at an emergency special session on the question of Palestine, after the killing of children in the war in Lebanon. It now recognises the pain of children everywhere who suffer physical, mental and emotional abuse in war.

WORLD_ELDER_ABUSE_AWARENESS_DAY.about: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day, on 15 June, was begun in 2006 by the International Network for the Prevention of Elder Abuse and recognised by the UN General Assembly in 2011. It draws attention to the neglect and the physical, mental and financial abuse that older people suffer. Senior citizens' groups in Nepal mark it with programmes on their rights and care.

INTERNATIONAL_DAY_FOR_THE_ELIMINATION_OF.about: The International Day for the Elimination of Sexual Violence in Conflict falls on 19 June, the date in 2008 when the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1820, which condemned sexual violence as a tactic of war. Proclaimed by the General Assembly in 2015, it honours survivors and calls for an end to such violence. In Nepal it is marked by survivors of the armed conflict and rights groups.

WORLD_YOUTH_SKILLS_DAY.about: World Youth Skills Day falls on 15 July. Proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 2014, it stresses the value of giving young people skills for work and enterprise through technical and vocational education and training. In Nepal technical schools and youth bodies mark it with skill exhibitions and programmes on employment.

WORLD_HEPATITIS_DAY.about: World Hepatitis Day, on 28 July, is the birthday of Baruch Blumberg, who discovered the hepatitis B virus and helped develop its vaccine. The World Health Assembly made it an official day in 2010 to raise awareness of viral hepatitis, which inflames the liver and can lead to cirrhosis and cancer. In Nepal it is marked with free testing, vaccination and talks.

WORLD_DAY_AGAINST_TRAFFICKING_IN_PERSONS.about: The World Day against Trafficking in Persons falls on 30 July. The UN General Assembly set it in 2013 to raise awareness of people trafficked for forced labour, sexual exploitation and other abuse, and to protect their rights. In Nepal, where trafficking across the open border and abroad for work is a long-standing concern, it is marked with rallies and awareness programmes.

WORLD_BREASTFEEDING_WEEK.about: World Breastfeeding Week runs from 1 to 7 August and has been kept since 1992 by the World Alliance for Breastfeeding Action with WHO and UNICEF. It recalls the Innocenti Declaration on breastfeeding of 1 August 1990. It promotes breastfeeding for a baby's health, and in Nepal health workers and mothers' groups mark it with counselling and programmes.

INTERNATIONAL_DAY_AGAINST_NUCLEAR_TESTS.about: The International Day against Nuclear Tests falls on 29 August, the date in 1991 when the Semipalatinsk nuclear test site in Kazakhstan was closed. The UN General Assembly proclaimed it in 2009, on Kazakhstan's proposal, to raise awareness of the harm of nuclear-weapon tests and to press for their end as a step toward a world without nuclear weapons.

INTERNATIONAL_DAY_OF_THE_VICTIMS_OF_ENFO.about: The International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances falls on 30 August. The UN General Assembly set it in 2010 to remember people taken by the state or its agents whose fate is hidden from their families. In Nepal, where more than a thousand people went missing during the armed conflict of 1996 to 2006, families of the disappeared hold vigils and demand truth and justice.

INTERNATIONAL_DAY_FOR_THE_PRESERVATION_O.about: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer falls on 16 September, the date in 1987 when the Montreal Protocol on substances that deplete the ozone layer was signed. Proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 1994, it marks the effort to protect the layer of ozone that shields the Earth from the Sun's ultraviolet rays. In Nepal it is marked with programmes and school events.

INTERNATIONAL_DAY_FOR_UNIVERSAL_ACCESS_T.about: The International Day for Universal Access to Information falls on 28 September. First proclaimed by UNESCO in 2015 and by the UN General Assembly in 2019, it affirms the public's right to seek and receive information held by public bodies. In Nepal, where the Right to Information Act has been in force since VS 2064, the National Information Commission and journalists hold programmes on it.

INTERNATIONAL_DAY_OF_NEUTRALITY.about: The International Day of Neutrality falls on 12 December, the date in 1995 when the UN General Assembly recognised Turkmenistan's permanent neutrality. Proclaimed by the Assembly in 2017, it promotes neutrality as a policy that helps keep peace and settle disputes through preventive diplomacy. It is marked mainly with diplomatic meetings and programmes.

WORLD_SUICIDE_PREVENTION_DAY.about: World Suicide Prevention Day, on 10 September, has been kept since 2003 by the International Association for Suicide Prevention with the World Health Organization. It aims to raise awareness that suicide can be prevented and to reduce the stigma around mental illness and seeking help. In Nepal mental-health groups mark it with talks and candlelight gatherings.

GLOBAL_TIGER_DAY.about: Global Tiger Day, on 29 July, was agreed at the tiger summit in St Petersburg in 2010, where the thirteen tiger-range countries, Nepal among them, pledged to double wild tiger numbers by 2022. Nepal's count rose from 121 in 2009 to 355 in 2022. National parks such as Chitwan and Bardiya and conservation groups mark it with rallies and programmes.

WORLD_LEPROSY_DAY.about: World Leprosy Day falls on the last Sunday of January. It was begun in 1954 by the French writer Raoul Follereau and is kept near 30 January, the anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi's death, in honour of his care for people with leprosy. It aims to end the disease and the stigma attached to it, and in Nepal is marked with screening camps and programmes.

INTERNATIONAL_DAY_OF_COOPERATIVES.about: The International Day of Cooperatives falls on the first Saturday of July. The International Co-operative Alliance has kept it since 1923, and the UN General Assembly recognised it in 1992. It honours cooperatives, businesses owned and run by their members. In Nepal, where savings and credit, dairy and farm cooperatives are widespread, it is marked with rallies and programmes.

INTERNATIONAL_DAY_OF_WOMEN_AND_GIRLS_IN_.about: The International Day of Women and Girls in Science falls on 11 February. Proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 2015, it presses for women's and girls' full and equal access to and part in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. In Nepal it is marked with talks by women scientists, school programmes and exhibitions.

WORLD_NGO_DAY.about: World NGO Day, on 27 February, honours non-governmental and non-profit organisations and the people who work and volunteer in them. It was declared by the Baltic Sea NGO Forum in 2010 and first kept worldwide in 2014. In Nepal, home to many thousands of registered NGOs, it is marked with programmes on civil society's role.

ZERO_DISCRIMINATION_DAY.about: Zero Discrimination Day, on 1 March, was begun by UNAIDS in 2014. First aimed at the discrimination faced by people living with HIV, it now promotes everyone's right to live a full life with dignity, free of discrimination in law and practice. In Nepal it is marked by HIV networks and rights groups with programmes and rallies.

WORLD_WILDLIFE_DAY.about: World Wildlife Day falls on 3 March, the date in 1973 when the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora was signed. Proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 2013, it celebrates wild animals and plants and draws attention to wildlife crime. In Nepal national parks and conservation groups mark it with programmes and exhibitions.

WORLD_POETRY_DAY.about: World Poetry Day, on 21 March, was proclaimed by UNESCO in 1999 to support the reading, writing, publishing and teaching of poetry and to give endangered languages a voice through it. Literary societies, schools and poets in Nepal mark it with poetry readings and gatherings in Nepali and the country's other languages.

INTERNATIONAL_TRANSGENDER_DAY_OF_VISIBIL.about: The International Transgender Day of Visibility, on 31 March, was begun in 2009 by the American activist Rachel Crandall-Crocker to celebrate transgender people and their contributions and to raise awareness of the discrimination they face. In Nepal, whose Supreme Court ordered legal recognition of a third gender in 2007, gender-minority groups mark it with gatherings.

INTERNATIONAL_DAY_OF_HUMAN_SPACE_FLIGHT.about: The International Day of Human Space Flight falls on 12 April, the date in 1961 when Yuri Gagarin of the Soviet Union became the first person to travel into space. Proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 2011, on the fiftieth anniversary of his flight, it marks the start of the space age for humankind and the use of outer space for peaceful ends.

WORLD_ART_DAY.about: World Art Day, on 15 April, is the birthday of Leonardo da Vinci. Proposed by the International Association of Art and proclaimed by UNESCO in 2019, it promotes the arts and the freedom of artists. In Nepal art galleries, the Nepal Academy of Fine Arts and art colleges mark it with exhibitions and live painting.

WORLD_IMMUNIZATION_WEEK.about: World Immunization Week is kept by the World Health Organization in the last week of April. Endorsed by the World Health Assembly in 2012, it promotes vaccines to protect people of all ages against diseases such as measles, polio and diphtheria. In Nepal, whose national immunization programme reaches children across the country, it is marked with vaccination drives and awareness.

INTERNATIONAL_DAY_OF_FAMILY_REMITTANCES.about: The International Day of Family Remittances falls on 16 June. Proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 2018, it recognises the money that migrant workers send home to support their families. In Nepal, where remittances from workers in the Gulf, Malaysia and India make up about a quarter of the economy, it is marked with programmes on migrants and the use of their earnings.

WORLD_PATIENT_SAFETY_DAY.about: World Patient Safety Day falls on 17 September. Established by the World Health Assembly in 2019, it aims to reduce the harm that patients suffer in health care through errors, unsafe practice and infection, and to involve patients and families in safer care. Hospitals and health workers in Nepal mark it with programmes and training.

INTERSEX_AWARENESS_DAY.about: Intersex Awareness Day, on 26 October, recalls the first public protest by intersex people in North America, held in Boston on 26 October 1996. It draws attention to people born with sex characteristics that do not fit typical definitions of male or female, and to their right to decide about their own bodies. In Nepal it is marked by gender and sexual minority groups.

WORLD_SCIENCE_DAY_FOR_PEACE_AND_DEVELOPM.about: World Science Day for Peace and Development falls on 10 November. Proclaimed by UNESCO in 2001 and first kept in 2002, it highlights the place of science in society and the need to involve the public in debates on science. In Nepal universities and science bodies mark it with talks and exhibitions.

WORLD_PNEUMONIA_DAY.about: World Pneumonia Day, on 12 November, was begun in 2009 by the Global Coalition against Child Pneumonia. Pneumonia is a leading infectious killer of young children, and the day presses for its prevention through vaccines, clean air and good nutrition, and for its prompt treatment. In Nepal health workers mark it with awareness programmes.

WORLD_PHILOSOPHY_DAY.about: World Philosophy Day falls on the third Thursday of November. Proclaimed by UNESCO in 2005, it honours philosophical thought and encourages people to share it and to use it in facing the questions of their time. In Nepal philosophy departments and societies mark it with talks on Eastern and Western thought.

WORLD_MEDITATION_DAY.about: World Meditation Day falls on 21 December, near the December solstice. The UN General Assembly proclaimed it in December 2024, on a proposal that Nepal joined in putting forward, to recognise meditation's benefits for mental and physical health. In Nepal meditation centres, monasteries and yoga groups mark it with group meditation sessions.

PASHUPATINATH_CHHAYA_DARSHAN.about: Pashupatinath Chhaya Darshan, the sight of the shadow, falls on the fourteenth day of Magh's bright half. After a special worship in which Newar devotees offer the linga a new crown, the courtyard on the temple's south side is filled with water, and the reflection of the Pashupatinath linga is shown in it to the public, who come in great numbers to see it.

BANEPA_CHANDESHWARI_JATRA.about: Banepa's chariot festival of Chandeshwari falls on the full moon of Baishakh, the day of Buddha Jayanti. The goddess Chandeshwari, whose temple stands above the town, is placed on her chariot and pulled through the streets of Banepa in Kavre over the days of the jatra, and families feast their relatives.

GURIYA_PARVA.about: Guriya Parva, the Tharu festival of the doll, is set by the national panchanga on the first of Shrawan, while many western Tharu keep it on Nag Panchami as Gurhi. Held after the rice is planted, it is told as keeping insects and disease from the crop: girls make dolls of cloth scraps, which the boys beat with sticks at a crossroads or pond, and the village shares a meal.

GURHI_PARVA.about: Gurhi, or Gurahi, is the festival of the western Tharu of Kailali, Kanchanpur, Bardiya, Banke and Dang, kept on Nag Panchami, the fifth day of Shrawan's bright half, after the rice planting. Girls make dolls from scraps of coloured cloth and the boys beat them with bamboo sticks, a rite told as driving insects and disease from the fields; Kailali's local governments make it a holiday.

RADHA_JANMOTSAV.about: Radha Janmotsav, Radha's birthday, falls on the eighth day of Bhadra's bright half, fifteen days after Krishna Janmashtami, and is also called Radhashtami. Vaishnavas, above all in Braj at Barsana, Radha's home, keep it with a fast until midday, worship of Radha and Krishna together, bhajans and processions; in Nepal Krishna's temples mark it.

NIMBARKACHARYA_JAYANTI.about: Nimbarkacharya Jayanti, which the national panchanga sets on the full moon of Kartik, honours Nimbarka, the teacher of the dvaitadvaita school, who taught the worship of Radha and Krishna together. His followers of the Nimbarka sampradaya, centred in Braj and Rajasthan, mark it at their temples with worship, bhajans and readings of his work.

AANPKO_MUJURA_KHANE_DIN.about: The day of rubbing on oil and eating mango blossom falls on the first day of Chaitra's dark half, the day after Holi's full moon, as spring sets in. It is the custom to oil the body and to pick and eat a little of the mango's flowering mujura, which is believed to help the mango crop to set and hold its fruit.

GANGAUR_PUJA_ARAMBHA.about: Gangaur Puja begins on the first day of Chaitra's dark half, the day after Holi, and runs for eighteen days to the third day of Chaitra's bright half. Kept above all by Rajasthani and Marwari women, it honours Gauri, Parvati: married women pray for their husbands' long life and unmarried girls for a good husband, worshipping clay images of Gauri and Shiva each day with songs.

NALA_MACHHINDRANATH_SNAN.about: Nala Machhindranath Snan, Nala Nhawan, falls on the first day of Chaitra's dark half, the day after Holi. At Nala, near Banepa in Kavre, the image of Karunamaya, held to be a form of Avalokiteshvara and worshipped as a giver of rain, is bathed with water, milk and honey to Newar music, in a rite of renewal before his jatra.

SARASWATI_AVAHAN.about: Saraswati Avahan, the invocation of Saraswati, falls in the Navaratri of Ashwin's bright half, on the day the Moon is in the nakshatra Mula. The goddess of learning is invoked into books, pens and instruments, which are set before her and worshipped; they rest from use until she is sent off a few days later, on the day of Shravana.

PHARPING_HARISHANKAR_JATRA.about: Pharping's Harishankar Jatra falls on the twelfth day of Ashwin's dark half, the day of the dwadashi shraddha, a few days before Dashain. In Pharping, south of Kathmandu, the chariots of the goddesses Dakshinkali, Nilbarahi and Indrayani and of Gopaleshwar are pulled through the town at night by its several communities.

RATO_MACHHINDRANATH_SNAN.about: Rato Machhindranath Snan, Bunga Dyah Nhawan, falls on the first day of Baishakh's dark half, some weeks before his chariot festival. The red image of Karunamaya, the god of rain, is brought from his temple to a platform at Lagankhel in Patan and bathed before great crowds; the god is then repainted and restored over the following days.

CHITTADHAR_HRIDAYA_JAYANTI.about: Chittadhar Hridaya Jayanti remembers the poet Chittadhar Hridaya, born Chittadhar Tuladhar in Kathmandu in 1906, a leading figure of the Nepal Bhasa renaissance and author of the epic Sugata Saurabha on the Buddha's life. It is kept by the lunar date of his birth, which falls on Apara Ekadashi, with readings and programmes in his memory.

MATINA_PARU.about: Matina Paru, Newar for 'love's first day', is the first day of Paush's dark half, the day after Yomari Punhi. Kirtipur keeps it as a day of feasting and visits, and it is told as a day when sweethearts and newly married couples exchange the yomari made for the full moon the evening before.

MANVADI_CHAITRA_SHUKLA_TRITIYA.about: The third day of Chaitra's bright half is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, when a bath, a shraddha and gifts are commended. It is also Gauri Tritiya, the closing day of Gangaur, when women who kept the eighteen days' worship of Gauri take her images in procession to the water.

MANVADI_CHAITRA_PURNIMA.about: The full moon of Chaitra is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, on which the texts commend a bath, a shraddha for the ancestors and gifts held to bring lasting merit. In much of northern India the same full moon is kept as Hanuman Jayanti.

MANVADI_JYESHTHA_PURNIMA.about: The full moon of Jestha is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, when a bath, a shraddha for the ancestors and gifts are commended. It is also the day of the Panauti bath at the confluence in Kavre, and in Odisha the day of Jagannath's bathing festival, Snana Purnima.

MANVADI_ASHADHA_SHUKLA_DASHAMI.about: The tenth day of Ashadh's bright half is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, when the texts commend a bath, a shraddha for the ancestors and gifts. It falls on the eve of Harishayani Ekadashi, when Vishnu's four months' sleep and the Chaturmas begin.

MANVADI_ASHADHA_PURNIMA.about: The full moon of Ashadh is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, on which a bath, a shraddha for the ancestors and gifts are commended. It is also Guru Purnima, the day of Vyasa, so the manvadi's rites are kept beside the honouring of teachers.

MANVADI_SHRAVANA_KRISHNA_ASHTAMI.about: The eighth of the dark half that follows Shrawan's full moon, which the texts count in Shrawan and Nepal's almanac in Bhadra, is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, when a bath, a shraddha and gifts are commended. It is the day of Krishna Janmashtami.

MANVADI_BHADRAPADA_SHUKLA_TRITIYA.about: The third day of Bhadra's bright half is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, when the texts commend a bath, a shraddha for the ancestors and gifts. It is also Haritalika, the day of the women's Teej fast, so in Nepal it is most widely known for that.

MANVADI_ASHWINA_SHUKLA_NAVAMI.about: The ninth day of Ashwin's bright half is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, on which the texts commend a bath, a shraddha for the ancestors and gifts. It falls on Maha Navami, the last of Dashain's nine nights, when Durga is worshipped and tools and vehicles are blessed.

MANVADI_KARTIKA_SHUKLA_DWADASHI.about: The twelfth day of Kartik's bright half is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, when the texts commend a bath, a shraddha and gifts. It follows Haribodhini Ekadashi, Vishnu's waking, so those who fasted break the fast this day; that evening Changunarayan's great lamp is lit.

MANVADI_KARTIKA_PURNIMA.about: The full moon of Kartik is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, on which the texts commend a bath, a shraddha and gifts. It closes Kartik Snan and the Chaturmas, so the manvadi's bath and offerings join the last bath of the month and the lighting of lamps.

MANVADI_PAUSHA_SHUKLA_EKADASHI.about: The eleventh day of Paush's bright half is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus. The texts commend a bath, a shraddha for the ancestors and gifts on each manvadi; this one falls on Putrada Ekadashi, so most who mark it also keep the ekadashi fast.

MANVADI_MAGHA_SHUKLA_SAPTAMI.about: The seventh day of Magh's bright half is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, when a bath, a shraddha and gifts are commended. It falls on Achala Saptami, the Sun's day, so its bath before sunrise and its offering to the rising Sun are kept together with the manvadi rites.

MANVADI_PHALGUNA_PURNIMA.about: The full moon of Phagun is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus, on which the texts commend a bath, a shraddha for the ancestors and gifts. It falls on Holi, Fagu Purnima, so the manvadi's bath and offerings are kept in the morning of a day otherwise given to colours.

MANVADI_PHALGUNA_AMAVASYA.about: The new moon that closes Phagun in the texts' reckoning, the one after Holi's full moon, is one of the fourteen manvadi days, each held to mark the beginning of the age of one of the fourteen Manus. As a new moon it is a day for the ancestors, and the texts commend a bath, a shraddha and gifts; in Nepal it is the new moon of Ghode Jatra.
